request: Remove the white LookDog logo from the homepage, or keep it top left if it should stay
recommendation: Keep it. The mark is navy #02244D and orange #F3741E - the site's own palette - and it is the home link. It was already top left. The white was not the logo, it was the background it was baked onto.

root_cause.effect: On the transparent homepage header the logo was a solid white rectangle on the hero photograph.

assets_built.content: the mark alone, centred on a square

method.trim: 32% of the original area was white margin. Trimmed to the content box before scaling.
method.knockout: Un-composited rather than colour-keyed: opacity from distance to white, original colour recovered by removing the white that was mixed in. Keeps antialiased edges clean instead of leaving a white fringe.
method.reverse: Orange kept, navy turned white. A reversed logo, not a recoloured one.
method.icon_crop: Found by reading the ink profile across the width - a clean empty column at about 37% separates the glyph from the wordmark.

four_places_pointed_at_the_old_file.effect: Put the full 688KB original into the 2x srcset slot on every page, so every visitor downloaded it regardless of screen.
Embedded the original directly in the footer.
A 1774x592 favicon. Favicons must be square, so it was never going to render properly.
Set to %site.icon%, so it inherited the same wrong file on every page.

also_fixed: The Organization schema carried a founder placeholder naming a Person after the site itself. Removed.

verification.favicon: lookdog-icon-100x100.png, generated from the square source
